problem: Dexterous warehouse tasks (picking, packing, kitting, receiving) remain manual.
business_model: Robots and models for warehouses (pricing model unknown)

founders.name: Oscar Brisset
previous_startups: Secondhand bookstore on eBay started at age 12 (outcome not stated)
founders.background_notes: AI engineer at BCG X and data engineer; a Pulse headline says he raised at 25 but no birth year given.

founders.name: Ben Kaye
education: Oxford, PhD in machine learning (YC); one source says he dropped out
founders.background_notes: Robotics master's and a patent-pending embedded systems invention per the YC launch post.

technical_complexity.rationale: Generalist dexterous manipulation on a two-armed wheeled platform with learned policies, custom data collection devices and no per-SKU retraining; research-adjacent, hardware plus ML.

defensibility.rationale: Value would come from manipulation data collected in 3PL sites, but well-funded picking and robot-foundation-model companies work the same problem; no moat shown yet.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early to say; the YC launch post targets 3PLs that big automation vendors ignore (the largest 10% of warehouses are their focus per IBTimes).

market_need_then: Piece picking has resisted automation for years (founder, IBTimes 2026-09). The YC launch post states existing automation costs $100-150K installed, and Remy claims half; first paying customer within four months of starting per IBTimes.

branding.domain_note: Uses tryremy.ai, a try- prefix on a .ai domain (date unknown).

brand_strength.rationale: Months old; no sourced press on the brand itself, and a name shared with other products.

outcome_analysis: Remy AI is a Winter 2026 two-founder Oxford team building a wheeled two-armed warehouse picking robot for e-commerce 3PLs, with a first paying customer reported within four months and research interest from Mitsubishi and Hyundai. It is too early for an outcome: funding is only reported at roughly $650K by one aggregator, with no verified round, exit or scale data.
notes: Directory Active, consistent. Funding unverified so no round recorded: Pulse (2026-04) reports $650K and a $500K YC investment, VCBacked about $700K, StartupHub $63M Series A (outlier, rejected), all aggregator or single-outlet. Competitor list comes from HUGE Magazine, a minor outlet dated March 2026; the YC Tier List also lists Physical Intelligence as adjacent (not recorded). Founders met at Oxford about seven years before the launch post. Kaye is described as dropping out of his PhD by one source and holding an Oxford ML PhD by YC; unresolved. Name origin not stated; no Ratatouille link claimed. Completeness pass: the roughly $650K raise (including $500K from YC) rests on a single outlet (Pulse); VCBacked says $700K and lists Oxford Seed Fund, YesPress says about $700K in January 2026.
